utterances.text: I don't remember that he came with us to Mostar. I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Very well. Now, tell me this, please: Do you know that Mr. Ganic, and this was something Mr. Karnavas asked you, at that time was a member of the Presidency of the Bosnia-Herzegovina, and as such occupying that post by the same token a member of the Supreme Command of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: BO PELLNAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I learnt today that he was not vice-president but member of the Presidency. Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Did he introduce himself to you as the vice-president?

utterances.speaker: BO PELLNAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe so.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. You said five minutes. I'm going on to discuss the documents so this would be a good time to break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We will now be breaking for 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Nozica.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Sir, can we discuss now matters which may have led to the conclusions taken at the meeting of the 18th of April and the reasons why some of these conclusions were made and look at some of the UNMO reports? I believe you have P 01965. That's the number of the document in the binder before you. This is the report by Mr. Ole Brix Andersen dated the 19th of April, 1993. Let us look at page 2 in the English version, in the middle of the page; which is page 2 of the Croatian version, and the beginning of that page. The Prosecutor had some questions for you concerning this document, but he skipped the part which said: "After lengthy, difficult, and sometimes tense discussions, three main issues were secured, three main conclusions were made," and the conclusions are explained here and it is said that all -- "each side, at a political level, accepted the absolute and immediate necessity of a cease-fire." It goes on to read that "on proposal of the chairman agreed by the UN military observers, UNPROFOR and every side, a separate meeting among the high level military representatives had to take place in order to agree on a concrete procedure for immediate and general cease-fire." "Brigadier Petkovic required the presence of BH army commander Mr. Halilovic at these talks, and the UNPROFOR commander promised that if possible Mr. Halilovic would be lifted to Mostar tomorrow by UN. Anyway, technical discussions could immediately begin." Mr. Ganic and Mr. Boras are mentioned here. They proposed that the investigation commissions at a high level comprised 6 members, two from each side and one from European Monitor's mission and this is something that transpires from the text. I will refer to the part shown you by the Prosecutor where Mr. Stojic is said to have appeared and is said to have indicated that a large scale offensive had been launched in Central Bosnia, especially in the areas of Vitez, Busovaca, Visoko, and Travnik. I don't believe that this part concerning Busovaca is true, but he says that in anticipation of further information the meeting was put off for the following day, if possible. They go on to talk about the objective of the meeting and about what had been achieved at the meeting. Can you recall, since you were there, that the agreement was that more information should be gathered about what was going on in the field and that the meeting should be put off for the following day?

utterances.speaker: BO PELLNAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I can't recall that because my memory from this meeting is the talks I had with General Petkovic, which was the most important thing for me, and then the impression made by Mr. Stojic is what has stayed in my memory. I don't remember how this meeting ended, and I do not remember that these agreements were made, but I don't dispute it in any way.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Yes, that's important. I would like to show you another document from this binder, which is document P 01981, and it's the sixth document from the top. This is another report by Mr. Ole Brix Andersen, dated the 20th of April, 1993. Let us look at page 5 of the English text, last sentence of that page, and then the text goes on to page 6. It is said that the first meeting that was held between the warring parties in Mostar was cut short by the HVO minister of defence who claimed that a large offensive had been launched by the BH army in Central Bosnia and the meeting was put off. It goes on to say, regardless of this, the main result was that -- was the establishment of two joint operation commissions consisting of ECMM, UNMO, HVO, and BiH in Mostar and Zenica. Therefore, this report speaks to the same event, does it not, that the meeting was in fact postponed?

utterances.speaker: BO PELLNAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But I am not completely sure that the key result about the joint operation commission actually was formulated during that meeting. I doubt that a bit, but I will not dispute that. It is possible.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: But this is stated in the reports. You said you fully accepted what the reports contain since you did not attend the whole meeting. You did not attend it from the beginning to end. Let us look at another document, which is P 01980. It's also contained in my binder, which is the ECMM weekly resume, or weekly summary. If you've found it, let us look at page 4.

utterances.speaker: BO PELLNAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not. Number again, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: 1980. This is in the Prosecutor's binder. Do you have the Prosecutor's binder before you? You used it yesterday. I didn't have time to move all these documents into my binder. 1980. It was also shown to you by the Prosecutor. Very well. Page 4 in English. The monitors of the European Community in all of their reports, including this one, on page 4 in English, indicate that the meeting had been put off in order to verify information about an offensive in Central Bosnia. They say, and I'm reading item 12. All the same, the key success achieved was the formation of the commission consisting of representatives of the ECMM," and so on and so forth, and a meeting of that commission was fixed for the 18th of April. Or, rather, it's first meeting is manned for the 18th of April.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: 19th of April.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And I suppose that this is the way things transpired. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: BO PELLNAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a document created by ECMM and probably written out of interest of ECMM. The fact I think I'm ready to acknowledge that this decision was taken. How it was taken and when it was taken, I am not willing to verify upon, but let's -- let's leave it by that. This decision obviously was taken during this day.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Thank you. Very well. Thank you. You said that in fact you didn't know why Mr. Stojic showed up at the meeting on the 18th of April, 1993. Did you have information about what was going on in the areas of Central Bosnia on the 17th, as you set out from Zagreb, and on the 18th as you arrived in Mostar? Did you obtain any information about the developments?

utterances.speaker: BO PELLNAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't answer that question. I don't know. I might have. I might not have.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: In that case, let us look at -- or, rather, let me ask you first whether you remember that Mr. Bruno Stojic had possibly brought along the document or something of that sort on the basis of which he presented his allegations about the start of an offensive in Central Bosnia. Can he -- you recall anything to that effect?

utterances.speaker: BO PELLNAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Please look at my document, 2D -- which is in my binder, 2D 00474, which is the third document from the bottom. This is the report dated the 17th of April, 1993. We see that it says at 1700 hours the report is sent by the Croatian Defence Council, operational zone Central Bosnia, command Vitez, and the subject is special report on terrorist attack and genocide against the Croatian people in Zenica (1700 hours). When we look at the document in the original, we can see that it's been written upon, and for the sake of the record I have to say that we received the document from the Prosecution. It contains an ERN number. Let us look at the text of the document. "From the terrorist act a few days ago when an HVO brigadier was kidnapped, Muslim extremists joined by other members of Muslim forces under the command by the 3rd Corps continue terrorising members of the HVO and the Croatian population." Let us stop here. Do you know that HVO members had been kidnapped and that the escorts of the brigadier were killed? Were you aware of this event which occurred -- the report only says a few days ago?

utterances.speaker: BO PELLNAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not at that moment, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Very well. "The full effect of terrorist actions occurred today," this is what the report says, on the 17th of April -- or rather, the 18th of April. "Muslim forces took control over all the important positions and they are killing civilians and HVO members by snipers and artillery. They are arresting and abusing Croats on a mass scale. The Mujahedins from Kozarac headed out towards Grm and Zmajevac, towards the HVO." Let us pay specific attention to Zmajevac because it will prove quite interesting later on. "The situation on the other -- in the other parts of Bosnia is unknown. Attacks at Cajdras was attempted from the direction of Lapac, but it was repelled. A T-55 tank is moving about the city, and another one went in the direction of Raspotovje and Drivusa. The 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade had taken -- had seized the Travnik street from where snipers are operating. The Muslim forces drove Croats out from the areas of Gornja Zenica, Luka, and they are also abandoning the village of Bilivode. "My estimation is the situation is going to deteriorate further and that many Croats will suffer during these actual and classical terrorist acts which are committed under the command by the highest -- under the command of the highest military level of the army of BH." Sir, do you recall from that meeting, where Mr. Bruno Stojic appeared, some mention was made of some of the events contained in this record or, rather, that he substantiated his statement concerning the BH army offensive partly by referring to what we have just read out in this report and that this happened at the time when you were present at the meeting.

utterances.speaker: BO PELLNAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't remember. Is this a verified document from that day, and is it the report from a military man?

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Yes, sir. You have his signature there. It says the chief of VOS, Operation Zone Central Bosnia, and it was sent to Mr. Dario Kordic, Mr. Tihomir Blaskic. We know where the document was obtained from, because in the original it says at the top, and we were given the document by the Prosecution. I cannot testify, but this is precisely the document that arrived on that critical date shortly before the meeting started. It was received by Mr. Stojic, and this was the immediate cause of his arrival at that meeting, and I'm wondering --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour. That's exactly --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: You have overlapped, Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: My apology for overlapping. Your Honour, counsel has just said she's not testifying but she just did. She's explained this document, stated her argument that Mr. Stojic had received exactly this document before bursting into the room and that's counsel. There is no evidence of this. Now, put a question to the witness and -- if they want to put that on in their own case they can try it. There is no evidence to support that. Please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Ms. Nozica. Please take Mr. Scott's comment into account.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes. I will take it into account. I was merely responding to the witness. I would not have discussed this had the witness not asked me where the document came from and whether it was verified. I was merely answering the witness's question.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Let us move on and look at what happened in Konjic, Jablanica and Zenica shortly before your arrival in Mostar and during your stay in Mostar. Perhaps ultimately we would be able to account for Mr. Stojic's arrival and his behaviour. Let's look at document P 1964, which is the document from my binder, the third document from the top. It is dated the -- I believe the document is under seal, and I would like us to go into private session. It was dated the 14th of April, 1993.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're back in open session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Sir, this is a document dated the 16th of April, 1993. You met with Mr. Ganic on the 17th of April, 1993. You were appointed to -- or, rather, you were tasked with going to Mostar together with him in order to calm down the tensions between Muslims and Croats. You said that you -- you didn't know that Mr. Ganic was a member of the Supreme Command. This is a document issued by the Supreme Command which was -- and was sent to the 4th Corps command and signed by head Fikret Muslimovic, or chief Fikret Muslimovic. The first paragraph is not relevant to our case at all. The second paragraph reads: "The central sphere of your work in these conditions has to be the protection of units and headquarters from the intelligence and other subversive activities which are being conducted based on the tasks given by the political centres from the territories of Herzegovina and Croatia, with a view to breaking up the sovereignty and --" now, look at this: "It is very important to gather data on all political, military, police and other activities which are carried out against the BH army. This because it is realistic to expect a further deterioration of relations and even a general military confrontation between the BH army and the HVO. It is very important for such a situation to make Muslims within the HVO as passive as possible and to influence their transfer from the HVO to the BH army." Sir, were you aware at the time that the HVO comprised large numbers of Muslims?

utterances.speaker: BO PELLNAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you say large numbers, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Well, let us specify. Were you aware of the fact that in Mostar itself there were Muslims in the HVO at the time? I will not give out any figures, but were you aware of the fact that in the month of April there were Muslims in the HVO in Mostar?

utterances.speaker: BO PELLNAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is -- if there were 2 or 200 has some importance, but I was not aware of it.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: But you knew that they were members of the HVO?

utterances.speaker: BO PELLNAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: But your question is useless unless there was a number which is politically significant. If there were two Muslims in the HVO in Mostar, then of course I didn't know about it. If there was 200, then it's interesting to know that I did not know about it.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Well, I will only conclude that it is quite interesting, the fact that you didn't know of them, because there was significantly more than two. Had there been more than two, Mr. Fikret Muslimovic or the Supreme Command Staff would not have issued such assignments as they did. Wouldn't you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: BO PELLNAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree with you on that point.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Did you know that at a later stage, let's say on the 30th of June, an attack took place launched by the BH army against the northern camp of Mostar and that it was carried out precisely in such a way that the Muslim members of the HVO from inside the army, the HVO, together with the BH army launched this attack, seized the barracks as well as Vrapcici and the western part of Mostar? Did you come by this information through the reports that you received later on?

utterances.speaker: BO PELLNAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not that I know of.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Let us look at the BH army activities in that period, which can be found in document P 01929. That's the first document in my binder. This document is signed by Mr. Arif Pasalic. The document is dated the 17th of April, 1993. This is an order sent to all the units of the 4th Corps. Were you aware of the fact that at the time the 4th Corps went all the way to Konjic, Jablanica? And I mean from Mostar all the way to those towns. Were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: BO PELLNAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yep.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: In point 1 it says: "Units in contact with the HVO and HV forces are obliged to continue their defence actions and all measures should be taken with that end in mind." And it says: "The centre of activity or focus of activity shall be on facilities and acts that endanger you most." Now, let's see how this order is interpreted. It says: "Initial successes should be maximally exploited and dominant features should be occupied from which you will be able to -- unless you have already occupied them from which you will be able to control larger territories and wider areas. Carry out mutual linking and coordination." So on the 17th of April, 1993, is the day before you met with Mr. Arif Pasalic, but at any rate, it was the day on which you met Mr. Ganic. And Mr. Arif Pasalic is issuing this order, from which we can see that the 4th Corps, even before this date, had carried out offensive action because underneath point 1 it says: "Take control of all dominant features unless you have already taken control of them," which means that they were supposed to have occupied them before this day, the 17th of April, 1993. Now, I assume you knew nothing about this when you arrived in Mostar. Do you agree with me there?

utterances.speaker: BO PELLNAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Can we now take a look at the next document, which is in my binder. It is 2D 00473. It is the 5th document from the back. It is an order once again. 2D 00473 is its number. Tell me when you've found it, please.

utterances.speaker: BO PELLNAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I got it.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: This is a Prosecution document once again, and it doesn't have an official date, but we do see that certain dates are mentioned in the document. It says to the commander RB 2/7 Motorised Brigade, and it is an order for attack. And I'll just look at several points which I'd like to refer you it. Number 2, for example, it says: "The 2/7th mountain brigade is to attack in the direction of Gradisce elevation 474 Zmajevac, and I'd like to mention Zmajevac in particular, because we have already had occasion to see that it was a point of interest to the 3rd and 4th Corps. Now once again in point 3 it goes on to say I have decided that the main access of attack is to be Gradisce elevation, et cetera, Zmajevac, the Zmajevac establishment, and then it says that readiness for the attack must be at 0500 hours on the 18th of April, 1993. And it says the focus of moral and political support must be to prepare the troops for executing the task and also to explain the intentions of the so-called Herceg-Bosna in compliance with an order issued by the command of the 3rd Corps dated the 17th of April, 1993, et cetera. And finally at the end it says in point 10 the commander of the brigade shall be held responsible support the execution of this order, the commander of the 2/7th Muslim Mountain Brigade. I assume you have heard of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade or perhaps not?

utterances.speaker: BO PELLNAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps not.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I'll nevertheless like to continue, although I don't see -- I can see that you don't know much of this, but let's get to the end to see what actually happened in the area, first of all with respect to the actions undertaken by the BH army. Now let us just take a look at document 2D 00472 briefly now. It is to be found in my binder, the sixth document from the back, and it is an elaboration of the previous document or details. It is an order for an attack dated the 17th of April, 1993, once again, and it says what the first guerrilla group should undertake, the second guerrilla group, and so on and so forth. Now, you have drawn your attention to the mention of Zmajevac in these documents precisely because in the document that I showed you previously, which was dated the 17th of April, 1993, an information report which was sent to Mr. Stojic, it precisely mentions that the Mujahedin from Kozarac have started out towards Grm and Zmajevac, and these orders by the BH army confirm what the details of this order of attack can -- are. Now, if we look at these orders, can we conclude from them, from the orders that we have looked at and the report that some of them were carried out, can we conclude that the BH army was indeed engaged in offensive action in Central Bosnia precisely on the day or one or two days before your arrival in Mostar? Is that something that becomes evident if you look at these orders?

utterances.speaker: BO PELLNAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was evident, because on some occasions the Croat -- the Croats in Mostar were extremely eager to re-establish communications with one of their units. So I suppose that they had been under attack and were isolated. So this is not nothing new to me. But please let me tell the Court that as a UN officer, you do not have intelligence resources at your disposal, nor do you do intelligence. And if you have it, you are very careful not to share it, because we could be used by the other party. So I think on the whole we had very little information about the formations, their numbers, and so on, and we didn't much care about it. So this is one reason why I may seem rather ignorant about the Mountain Brigade and so on. We really stayed out of that business. You may have go to the Brits or the Americans to get better information.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Sir, the aim of my examination was not to see whether you knew about some units. Some units were certainly important and had high-sounding names and are mentioned. However, I have shown you the documents because I wanted to show you what happened, what was going on at that point in time in that area and to link that up with the requests and demands made and to see whether they were justified or not, that in your mission you take into account all the events up there, and as you said at the beginning put them on a par, on the same level. Now, let's see the manner in which the BH army was behaving at the time when negotiations were undertaken with you and your offers considered. Now, for purposes of continuity, let us look at 3D 00559. To -- it is the last document in my binder. 00559 is the document number. 3D.

utterances.speaker: BO PELLNAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: You can take a look at the English translation. It is on page 2 it, but it is the agreement on the 18th of April, 1993, signed by Alija Izetbegovic and Mate Boban. So that is the day of your arrival and of your meetings, and we'll read it through briefly. "All disagreements," point 1, "regarding the relation between the Croat and Muslim people of Bosnia-Herzegovina must be solved through political means. "2. There is no reason for hostilities between the BH army and the Croatian Defence Council. "3. We order all units to cease hostilities immediately, release prisoners and through negotiation at all levels to remove the causes of conflict. "4. Immediately establish responsibility in the aims of units and individuals for the beginning of the hostilities." Now, I assume you haven't seen this document before, but am I right in reading out what it says here?

utterances.speaker: BO PELLNAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I might well have seen this document since it is this Security Council -- from the Secretary-General would most certainly have been circulated within UNPROFOR. So I -- I should have seen it, actually.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: So, sir, the day -- the date of the document is the 18th of April, and on the 19th of April you and Mr. Ganic were in Mostar. You discussed the situation. I know that there were other persons present, too, but I am highlighting Mr. Ganic here, and you were negotiating about a cessation to the hostilities in Mostar and for that reason and upon Mr. Ganic's insistence that is the reason you came to Mostar in the first place. But now let's take a look at another document which at that time was compiled in Mostar. It is document P 01970. And in my binder it is the fifth document from the top. We have seen this document several times in court, but let's look at -- look at it together now in a different light, from a different angle this time. Tell me when you've found it, please.

utterances.speaker: BO PELLNAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I got it.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Yes. This document was issued by the command of the 41st Motorised Brigade. You don't have to know that, but please believe me when I say that it was located in the town of Mostar. The document is dated the 19th of April, 1993, and it is an order. It says: "An order for defence," up at the top, and then it says: "I hereby order," and I'd just like to remind you of the most important point. "All units of the 41st Motorised Brigade" it says, as well as elements of units from the composition of the 4th Corps should take up positions for decisive defence with the task of defending allocated regions as follows. So without doubt and I'm sure you can confirm this, that on that date, the 19th of April, you did have contacts with Mr. Arif Pasalic who was the commander of the 4th Corps; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: BO PELLNAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And we can also conclude that Mr. Ganic, who was a member of the Supreme Command of the BH army at that point in time was in Mostar on a peace mission to establish a truce between the Croats and the Muslims with special emphasis on Mostar where you were highly involved; am I right?

utterances.speaker: BO PELLNAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, he seems to have every reason to be there. It looks to me he had every reason to be there when I read this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Yes. I think our conclusions are the same. And once we have seen the document I'm sure our positions will be identical. Now, I'm going to skip certain portions and look at point 1.3 of this order, 1.3 where it says the following: "The 3rd Battalion has the task of taking up defence positions in their area of responsibility closing down the axis from Vrapcici towards Mostar in the region of Sutina and preventing the crossing over of the hydroelectric power plant of Mostar, the dam, as well as totally blocking and capturing the North Camp barracks." This is the barracks that I asked you about earlier on about the events of the 30th of June, and you couldn't remember. However, it is a very significant order, because it is linked up with the events of the order of Mr. Muslimovic of the 16th of April where people are mentioned, Muslims mentioned in HVO units, and here once again we have an order to attack North Camp, and it was indeed attacked on the 30th of June as the documents bear out. It says: "Part of the troops with weaponry should be transferred to the right bank and placed under the command of the 2nd Battalion commander. Dispatch the complete crew for RBR Osa crew and containers as well as the crew for the RPG, rocket grenade launcher's crew. They should be trained in the use of the weapons they have." Now I'd like to draw your attention to point 1.8. 1.8. I'm sure you will remember something linked to this particular portion. It says: "The MUP of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina has the task of taking up positions and defending the Old Bridge and the newly-built bridge on Musala. With elements of the forces, launch an attack on the MUP premises and the Mostar police station, capture them and defend them fiercely. Aim to keep the Hirurgija surgery building in our zone. The troops to be used in the attack on the MUP building and the Mostar police station are to be on standby in the Mostar Hotel." So this order, sir, is dated the 19th of April, 1993, and yesterday you said that with respect to moving members of the BH army from the Mostar Hotel, that you had members with the -- problems with the members of the BH army and that Mr. Arif Pasalic was very reluctant to carry it out. Now, is the situation clearer to you now? It was precisely when you were engaged in those activities that Mr. Hujdur, the commander of the 41st Motorised Brigade, together with Mr. Arif Pasalic, issued an order, an offensive order, for this unit to go into operation, the unit that was at the Mostar Hotel. Now, does it seem to you be logical? Do you see the logics of why they resisted leaving the building so much? Do you see the reason for that now?

utterances.speaker: BO PELLNAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I don't see the reason, because Arif Pasalic agreed to take them out, and he went with me and we took them out. So I -- I would say that if this order was in -- actually issued on the 19th, it is highly strange that the commanding officer of the 4th Corps would go with me and bring out the soldiers from the Mostar -- Hotel Mostar, which he actually did. So I don't see it at all, actually. And there's one other question. This order is issued on the 19th, and you say we attacked on the barracks occurred on the 30th of June. So I fail to see the connection with it as well. If there is a connection, it took them a hell of a long time to launch that attack.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Sir, the first point is this: You said yesterday, or you told us the circumstances under which the members of the unit from Mostar moved out, and you said that the reason was because the Croatian side insisted upon it. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: BO PELLNAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: You said that you told Mr. Arif Pasalic that you were ready to carry out the operation, and you invited him to do so.

utterances.speaker: BO PELLNAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: You said that the number of members of the BH army in the hotel increased constantly, although the initial assessment of Mr. Pasalic, what he told you was that there were only 30 to 35 soldiers there; is that right?

utterances.speaker: BO PELLNAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now, you said yesterday during the examination-in-chief that Mr. Arif Pasalic did not show any enthusiasm on that score, and that you had to almost push those soldiers out of the Mostar Hotel.

utterances.speaker: BO PELLNAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I got the impression that he was more scared of his soldier than I was. He -- he was very weak commanding at that time. I think he was only too happy that we did the work for him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam Nozica, we have to finish. It's a quarter to. There's a new trial coming, and those who follow us are not pleased if there is any delay. So tomorrow we will continue, we will resume tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as I know, there is no other hearing in this courtroom this afternoon. Might I just be allowed to finish this document and then we can move on to the next document tomorrow?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. So if you tell me there is no other hearing, all right, then you can continue and finish. No, there is another hearing, and Judge Mindua has also another hearing. So we will --

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, it was my information that the Srebrenica trial was not ongoing this week, but I won't insist. Thank you. I'll continue tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. So, General, you will come back to the next hearing, tomorrow at 9.00, and that will be your last day. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 7th day of June, 2007, at 9.00 a.m. 18 19 20 21 22 23 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.46 p.m.,
